It has the school's padlock, and under that a second, smaller one that is not the school's. Chalked low on the plate, where only someone kneeling would see it: a little spiral, drawn in one line — a helix. The dust on the floor in front of the housing has two knee-prints in it.
c_m9_junction.journal: The old projector housing in the plant under the Trial Domes has a second private padlock and a small chalk helix on it.

c_m9_notebook.text: A notebook bound in grey linen, the corners worn round. A woman's fast upright hand. Page after page of a projector unlike the ones in the domes: coils wound in a double spiral, the beam folded back through itself. On one page she has drawn a hologram hero leaning on the edge of a table — and shaded the table edge where the hand presses it. In the margin: 'It holds. God help me, it holds.' On the facing page, boxed twice: 'Needs the K.A. pigment. Nothing else carries it. Remember the ink room. DO NOT BUILD. — M.'
c_m9_notebook.journal: A grey linen notebook in a woman's hand describes a projector that makes holograms solid, says it needs 'the K.A. pigment', and ends: 'DO NOT BUILD. — M.'

c_m9_night_walks.text: Dmitri, from his porch chair, not unkindly: twice a week, a little after one, the door of Bungalow 4 opens and Leona goes up the boardwalk with a torch she does not switch on. She is back before five. Once she had rust to the elbow of her cardigan; once, brick dust in her hair; once she was carrying her shoes. "She walks like somebody who has practised walking quietly," he says. "Most people here haven't had to."
c_m9_night_walks.journal: Leona leaves Bungalow 4 after one in the morning twice a week with an unlit torch and comes back before five, sometimes with rust or brick dust on her.

c_m9_rig.text: Maisie's rig on the porch of Bungalow 4 is an arcade emitter, a lighthouse lens and a great deal of solder. It throws a Debt-O-Tron the size of a cat, flat and flickering like every hologram on the island. Then a first-print card comes within a hand's breadth of the coil. The flicker stops. The little machine turns its head, takes one step — and a loose screw rolls off the bench, pushed. Maisie's welding goggles are on her forehead and her mouth is open. "It pushed back," she says. "Do that again. Don't do that again. Do that again."
c_m9_rig.journal: Next to a first-print card, the hologram from Maisie's rig stopped flickering and pushed a screw off the bench.

c_m9_argument.text: Two voices behind a door that is not quite shut, both kept low, which makes it worse. Hers: "You sold her." His: "I sold paper. To keep her breathing." Hers: "And did she?" A long silence. His, almost inaudible: "You forged my name, Leona." "You let it stand." "Yes." Something is set down on a bench, carefully. "He has two-fifths. He will not get the rest while I am alive." "That's not the same as him not getting it."
c_m9_argument.journal: Overheard Leona and Professor Helical: he sold 'paper' to pay for someone's treatment; she forged his name; someone has 'two-fifths' and wants the rest.

c_m9_two_fifths.text: Selene, on what the grey suit says into his telephone in the steam: "'I own two-fifths of a dead woman's idea and the widower is sitting on the other three.' Then: 'No, he'll hand them over. The daughter's admission is a forgery — the boy in the gloves found the page. A father will do a great deal to keep a girl from being put on a boat.' He asked me for a fresh towel in the same voice."
c_m9_two_fifths.journal: Selene overheard Marrow: he owns 'two-fifths of a dead woman's idea', and means to get the rest by threatening 'the daughter's' forged admission.

c_m1_printed_clean.text: Victoria Capulet, on her bench, parasol across her knees, watching the terraces with the same grave attention she gives to card art. {H} passes below. "That {H:boy} is printed too clean," she says, to nobody, in her clear carrying voice. "There is no line round {H:him}. And {H:his} shadow is late. It is unpunctual of it." Two people nearby smile at each other. {H} stops, looks up at her, and says, with every appearance of sincerity, "I apologise. I am working on it." She inclines her head, satisfied.
c_m1_printed_clean.journal: Victoria remarked aloud that {H} is 'printed too clean', has 'no line round {H:him}', and that {H:his} shadow is late. {H:He} apologised to her.

c_m1_dmitri_log.text: {H=@near?Dmitri keeps a notebook of the row at night, because he is awake and it passes the time. He turns it round for you. Every night since the meteor, one line the same: '02:10 — {H:ini} under the window of 7, no sound. Then to the waterline. Stands.' You look for the line where {H} goes home. Dmitri shakes his head. "I never see her go. I don't sleep, and I never see it. And in the morning she is sitting on your steps."|Dmitri keeps a notebook of the row at night, because he is awake and it passes the time. He turns it round for you. Every night since the meteor, one line the same: '02:10 — door of 7, no sound. {H:ini} to the waterline. Stands.' You look for the line where {H} comes back. Dmitri shakes his head. "I never see him come back. I don't sleep, and I never see it. And in the morning he walks out of your door to breakfast."}
c_m1_dmitri_log.journal: {H=@near?Dmitri logs {H} standing under my window at 02:10 every night and then at the waterline, and has never once seen her leave.|Dmitri logs {H} walking to the waterline at 02:10 every night and has never once seen him return, though he is inside by morning.}

c_m1_plank_wall.text: Bungalow 6 shares a plank wall with yours. They used to bang on it about the snoring. Tobias, mouth full: there's no snoring now — there's no anything; he put his ear to the boards and couldn't hear a person breathe. So for a laugh he knocked: shave-and-a-haircut. The answer came back at once, the same five knocks, same weight, same gaps. He tried a different rhythm. "It came back before I'd finished," he says, and stops chewing. Sammy has moved his bed to the far wall and says it's for the light.
c_m1_plank_wall.journal: The boys in Bungalow 6 hear no snoring and no breathing through the wall. When Tobias knocked, his knock was returned exactly — once before he had finished it.

c_m1_bees.text: Trixie is on her knees in the sand below the eaves of Bungalow 2 with a matchbox. Her bees have changed their flight line: they leave the bee hotel, go out over the water in a wide arc and come in again at the far end of the row. The arc bends round one bungalow. "Some of them forget," she says, very small, not sunny at all, and opens the matchbox. Seven bees, dead, laid out by her in a row as she found them under your window — and she found them, she says, all pointing the same way. Up the mountain.
c_m1_bees.journal: Trixie's bees now fly a wide arc around Bungalow 7. The ones she finds dead under its window all point toward the mountain.

c_m1_meat.text: Hedda went for {H} across the supper table over a plate of ribs — megaphone, 'murderer', the full sermon. {H:He} heard her out with total attention and asked, "Is this a conflict?" She said it certainly was. He thought about that. "You are in conflict with everyone," he said. "That cannot be the kind they mean." But he put the rib down all the same. He has not eaten meat since; some days he has not eaten. "I have stopped," he told her the next morning. "Is it over?" Hedda, who has waited her whole life for someone to give in that completely, cannot explain why it made her want to cry. Rafa says the gulls on the breakwater will not take scraps from a plate he has touched.
c_m1_meat.journal: When Hedda attacked {H} for eating meat {H:he} asked 'Is this a conflict?', stopped at once, and asked the next day 'Is it over?'

c_m1_aquavit.text: Freya can drink the row under the boardwalk and says so. At the fire she handed {H} her bottle of aquavit as a dare. He drank it the way you drink water after a run — all of it, in one, without his eyes watering — and handed it back empty. Then he sat and waited, politely, hands on his knees. After a minute he asked her, "When does it begin?" She leaned in to smell his breath, laughing. She stopped laughing. "Nothing," she says. "Not even the caraway."
c_m1_aquavit.journal: {H} drank a whole bottle of Freya's aquavit without effect and asked 'When does it begin?'. {H:His} breath did not smell of it.

c_m1_wearing_someone.text: Fiona works hard at being unsettling — the voice, the lace, the stare — and three boys adore her for it. Out of the make-up, on the steps of Bungalow 4, she tells you about the one thing on this island she calls wrong — 'not eerie; eerie is a costume'. {H} stopped in front of her, studied her face from very close, and said with real warmth: "You are wearing someone as well. It is very well done." Then he asked whether it was tiring. "I said yes," she says. "I don't know why I told him the truth. He nodded like we were colleagues."
c_m1_wearing_someone.journal: {H} told Fiona, admiringly, that she is 'wearing someone as well', and asked whether it was tiring.
